title: test-0058-SOC-CIV-ELECTIONS
passage: In India, the country is divided into different areas for the purpose of elections, which are called electoral constituencies. These boundaries are not determined by the physical size of the land, but by the population living in each region to ensure fair representation. Once these areas are fixed, the Election Commission of India prepares a voters' list, which is a complete record of all eligible citizens who can cast their ballots. The Election Commission functions as an independent constitutional body, meaning it operates entirely separately from the ruling government or the Prime Minister's office. Its primary role is to ensure that the electoral process remains free and fair for everyone. In certain areas, some constituencies are reserved for people belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. It is important to note that in these reserved areas, all eligible voters living in that constituency, regardless of their own caste, have the right to vote. The goal of these elections is not merely to pick a popular celebrity, but to allow citizens to choose representatives who will make laws and govern the country effectively. By following this structured process, the system ensures that every vote carries equal weight and the democratic spirit of the nation is upheld.
